audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for voyage to Rome, storm, Paul warning, angelic assurance, shipwreck, Eucharistic meal imagery, all saved/healed alive.

verses.restored: When it was decided that we should sail away to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius of the Augustan cohort.

familiar.text: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

verses.restored: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium about to sail to places along Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus a Macedonian from Thessalonica being with us.

familiar.text: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

verses.restored: The next day we put in at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to friends to receive care.

familiar.text: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

verses.restored: Putting out from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus because the winds were contrary.

familiar.text: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

verses.restored: Sailing through the sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra of Lycia.

familiar.text: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

verses.restored: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy and put us aboard it.

familiar.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

verses.restored: Sailing slowly for many days and coming with difficulty off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us, we sailed under the lee of Crete off Salmone.

familiar.text: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

verses.restored: Coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city Lasea.

familiar.text: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

verses.restored: Since considerable time had passed and the voyage was already dangerous, because even the Fast had already gone by, Paul advised them,

familiar.text: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,

verses.restored: saying to them, Men, I behold that the voyage is about to be with hardship and much loss, not only of cargo and ship, but also of our lives/souls.

familiar.text: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

verses.restored: But the centurion was persuaded more by the pilot and shipowner than by the things spoken by Paul.

familiar.text: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

verses.restored: Because the harbor was unsuitable for wintering, the majority advised putting out from there, if somehow they might reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest, and winter there.

familiar.text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

verses.restored: When a south wind blew gently, supposing they had obtained their purpose, they lifted anchor and sailed along Crete close inshore.

familiar.text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.

verses.restored: Not long after, a violent wind called the Northeaster rushed down from it.

familiar.text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

verses.restored: The ship was caught and not able to face the wind, so giving way, we were driven.

familiar.text: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

verses.restored: Running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were barely able to secure the skiff.

familiar.text: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

verses.restored: After hoisting it, they used helps to undergird the ship. Fearing they might run aground on the Syrtis, lowering the gear, they were driven.

familiar.text: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

verses.restored: Being violently storm-tossed, the next day they began throwing cargo overboard.

familiar.text: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

verses.restored: On the third day they threw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands.

familiar.text: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

verses.restored: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm lay upon us, from then on all hope that we would be saved/healed was being taken away.

familiar.text: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

verses.restored: After much abstinence from food, Paul stood in their midst and said, Men, you should indeed have obeyed me and not put out from Crete, and so avoided this hardship and loss.

familiar.text: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

verses.restored: And now I urge you to take courage, for there will be no loss of life/soul among you, but only of the ship.

familiar.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.

verses.restored: For this night a messenger of the Divine to whom I belong and whom I serve stood by me,

familiar.text: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

verses.restored: saying, Do not fear, Paul; it is necessary for you to stand before Caesar. And look, the Divine has graciously given you all those sailing with you.

familiar.text: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

verses.restored: Therefore take courage, men, for I trust the Divine that it will be thus, according to the way it has been spoken to me.

familiar.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.restored: But it is necessary for us to run aground on some island.

familiar.text: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

verses.restored: When the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic, around midnight the sailors suspected that some land was approaching them.

familiar.text: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

verses.restored: Taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms; going a little farther, again taking soundings, they found fifteen fathoms.

familiar.text: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

verses.restored: Fearing we might run somewhere onto rocky places, they threw four anchors from the stern and were praying for day to come.

familiar.text: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

verses.restored: As the sailors were seeking to flee from the ship and had lowered the skiff into the sea under pretense of laying out anchors from the bow,

familiar.text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

verses.restored: Paul said to the centurion and soldiers, Unless these remain in the ship, you are not able to be saved/healed.

familiar.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

verses.restored: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall off.

familiar.text: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

verses.restored: Until day was about to come, Paul was urging all to take food, saying, Today is the fourteenth day you have continued waiting without food, taking nothing.

familiar.text: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

verses.restored: Therefore I urge you to take food, for this is for your saving/healing; for not a hair from the head of any of you will perish.

familiar.text: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

verses.restored: Saying these things and taking bread, he gave thanks to the Divine before all, and breaking it, began to eat.

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

verses.restored: All became encouraged, and they themselves took food.

familiar.text: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

verses.restored: We were in all two hundred seventy-six souls/lives in the ship.

familiar.text: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

verses.restored: Having been satisfied with food, they lightened the ship, throwing the wheat into the sea.

familiar.text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

verses.restored: When day came, they did not recognize the land, but noticed a certain bay with a beach, onto which they planned, if able, to drive the ship.

familiar.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

verses.restored: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosening the bands of the rudders, and raising the foresail to the wind, they held toward the beach.

familiar.text: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

verses.restored: But striking a place between two seas, they ran the vessel aground. The bow stuck and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken by the force of the waves.

familiar.text: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

verses.restored: The soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any, swimming away, should escape.

familiar.text: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

verses.restored: But the centurion, wishing to save/heal Paul, prevented them from their intention and commanded those able to swim to throw themselves off first and get to land,

familiar.text: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:

verses.restored: and the rest, some on planks and some on things from the ship. And thus it happened that all were brought safely through onto the land.

familiar.text: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
